sources.citation: Kashoki, Mubanga E. & Michael Mann. 1978. A general sketch of the Bantu languages of Zambia. In S. Ohannessian & M. E. Kashoki (eds.), Language in Zambia, 47-100. London: International African Institute.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: General statement for Zambian Bantu languages, not Simaa-specific (printed p.70, sec. 3.4 Tone and Stress): 'In Zambian languages, in contrast, syllables are more or less evenly stressed.. In some languages, however, (e.g. Cewa) the penultimate syllable seems to be pronounced with slightly greater force.. stress in Zambian languages does not distinguish words from each other in meaning.' Simaa is mentioned only in the speaker tables, Fortune's lexicostatistic chart (p.59) and for having dental fricatives (p.68).

sources.citation: Wikipedia 'Simaa language' and Glottolog 5.x languoid records sima1258 / mwen1238 (meds: Yukawa 1987; Lisimba 1982; Fortune 1963; Kula 2012 for Mwenyi)
sources.note: Nothing; used only to establish the dialect set (Imilangu, Liyuwa, Makoma, Mulonga, Mwenyi, Nuclear Simaa, Nyengo) and the bibliography.

sources.citation: Yukawa, Yasutoshi. 1987. A Tonological Study of Mwenyi Verbs. In Y. Yukawa, J. H. Simooya & R. Kagaya (eds.), Studies in Zambian Languages (Bantu Linguistics, ILCAA, vol. 1), 35-72. Tokyo: ILCAA, Tokyo University of Foreign Studies. [Glottolog ref 139795; open at https://tufs.repo.nii.ac.jp/records/11523]
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. The paper treats Mwenyi (a western Luyana dialect, grouped by Glottolog under Simaa) as a two-tone language: p.36 'Although the convention does not use any tone mark, an acute is put on the high-toned vowel and nothing on the low-toned vowel in this paper'; verbs fall into two tonal groups (A/B) and every tense form is given a H/L tonal representation. No mention of stress, accent placement, penultimate lengthening or prominence anywhere in the 38 pages (scanned a full-text search for stress/accent/penult/promin/length: no hits; intro pp.35-40 and pp.69-72 read in full).

sources.citation: 湯川恭敏 [Yukawa Yasutoshi]. 1987. ムエニ語動詞アクセント試論 / A Tentative Tonal Analysis of Mwenyi Verbs. アジア・アフリカ文法研究 (Asian & African grammatical studies, ILCAA) 16: 1-44. [expanded Japanese version of the English paper; open at https://tufs.repo.nii.ac.jp/records/11652]
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Image-only PDF, no Japanese scanned by automated download; pp.1-2 read visually. 'アクセント' is used in Yukawa's sense of lexical pitch (tone): p.2 '慣用ではアクセントを表記することはしないが、ここでは、高く発音される母音の上に´をつけ、低く発音される母音には何もつけない' (= high-pitched vowels marked with acute, low unmarked). Same content as the English intro; no stress statement seen. Body (pp.3-44) is tonal paradigms, not read page by page.

sources.citation: Kula, Nancy C. 2015. A preliminary documentation of Siluyana: comparing Mbowe and Mwenyi. ELAR deposit SG0118; bundle 'Sound system', file 'Basic sound system'; consultant Muyambango Kaywa, Lusaka 2015-11-06).
